newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch seize record haul of pirate CDs.
newsitem.headline: Dutch seize record haul of pirate CDs.

text.p: Officials at Amsterdam's Schiphol Airport said on Wednesday they seized 96,000 illegal compact discs (CDs) in a shipment from Bulgaria last Friday.
Dutch Customs and the Dutch Authors' Society Buma/Stemra said the pirate CDs with a total retail value of $2.4 million were probably destined for the European market.
"The catch, which includes the brand new repertoire of U2, No Doubt and David Bowie, is the biggest ever seizure of counterfeit CDs in the Netherlands," they said in a joint statement.
They said customs officials at Schiphol became suspicious about a huge shipment of CDs from Bulgaria, the world's second largest producer of pirate CDs after China.
Customs and Buma/Stemra recently concluded a memorandum which increases their co-operation in clamping down on illegal audio-visual products.
The music industry has asked the European Commission to urge Bulgaria to stop producing pirate CDs, saying it costs the industry $100 million a year.
It has estimated that the former communist nation produces 15 million CDs a year.
Worldwide piracy cost the music industry $2.1 billion in 1995, of which $1 billion was in Europe.
